title: Technology Trends with Life Sciences Implications
summary: Life sciences perspective on technology trends covering the convergence of strategy and technology, disappearing physical-virtual boundaries, and data sharing imperatives for the industry.

findings.strategy_technology_inseparability: Technology and business strategy are becoming inseparable in life sciences. Organizations where CTO/CDO functions are integrated with business strategy show faster time-to-value on technology investments.
findings.physical_virtual_convergence: The boundary between physical and virtual worlds is disappearing. For life sciences: virtual clinical trial visits, AR-guided manufacturing, digital twin drug modeling, and hybrid HCP engagement blur traditional distinctions.
findings.data_sharing_foundation: Data-sharing platforms must facilitate trust among collaborators. Requirements: data availability and accuracy, security, ease of use, appropriate use policies. Creating a business case for each collaboration requires defining shared purpose, confidentiality requirements, and controls.
findings.data_privacy_governance: Proper governance, compliance, privacy, and security boundaries are prerequisites for data sharing. Life sciences faces heightened requirements due to: patient data sensitivity, IP protection for R&D data, regulatory reporting obligations, and cross-border data transfer restrictions.
findings.disruption_timeline: These trends are expected to cause significant disruption within 18-24 months. Forward-thinking organizations are investing now in foundational capabilities rather than waiting for proven approaches.

source: Technology trends report providing a life sciences perspective on strategy-technology convergence, data sharing, and physical-virtual boundaries
